title: Event Sourcing & CQRS Core Engine with Optimistic Concurrency Control
problem: Traditional relational CRUD architectures mutate state in-place, permanently discarding historical context regarding how and why data changed. Debugging concurrency race conditions, proving complete regulatory audit trails, and executing temporal queries become impossible once previous states are overwritten. This project implements a production Event Sourcing and Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS) framework in TypeScript and Node.js with PostgreSQL and Kafka. The system records all domain state changes as an immutable append-only sequence of domain events, enforces optimistic concurrency control via sequence revision checking, creates periodic aggregate snapshots to bound replay time, projects domain events into query-optimized read models, and exposes a temporal query engine capable of replaying entity state to any historical millisecond.
use_cases: Financial banking systems requiring immutable audit trails of every balance-impacting event
Supply chain logistics platforms tracking historical ownership transfers and custody changes
Complex domain-driven design applications requiring historical time-travel state reconstruction
hard_parts: Enforcing optimistic concurrency control in the append-only event store to prevent concurrent write split-brain
Maintaining exactly-once projection updates from asynchronous Kafka event streams into query read models
Designing aggregate snapshotting and event replay mechanisms that reconstruct state in sub-10 milliseconds
Handling temporal time-travel queries by projecting domain events up to an arbitrary historical timestamp
screener_signals: Clean TypeScript codebase cleanly separating event store, aggregate roots, projections, and CQRS commands
Automated concurrency race test asserting 100% collision rejection when two writes target identical aggregate revisions
Anti-fake verification script appending dynamic events, executing historical replay, and asserting exact state reconstruction

components.name: Append-Only Event Store
components.purpose: Persists immutable domain events with unique sequence revisions, enforcing optimistic concurrency

components.name: Aggregate Root Base & Concurrency Guard
components.purpose: Encapsulates business domain invariants, handles command dispatch, and applies internal event handlers

components.name: Kafka Event Streaming Dispatcher
components.purpose: Publishes newly appended domain events from event store to Kafka topics in strict sequence order

components.name: Read-Model Projection Worker
components.purpose: Consumes domain events from Kafka and builds materialized, denormalized read views for fast queries

components.name: Snapshot & Temporal Replay Engine
components.purpose: Creates aggregate state snapshots every 100 events and reconstructs entity state at any point in time

architecture.data_flow: Commands arrive at the CQRS Command Gateway; the target Aggregate Root loads its latest snapshot and replays subsequent events from the Append-Only Event Store; the aggregate validates business invariants and produces new domain events; the Event Store attempts to commit events with the expected aggregate version; if a concurrent write modified the version, an OptimisticConcurrencyError terminates the transaction; on success, the Kafka Dispatcher publishes committed events; the Read-Model Projection Worker updates denormalized tables; temporal queries reconstruct historical state by replaying events up to the requested timestamp.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Unique compound database constraint on (aggregate_id, version) rejecting concurrent race writes; immutable event tables preventing updates or deletes.

prerequisites: Proficiency in TypeScript, asynchronous Node.js, and SQL relational databases
Understanding of Domain-Driven Design concepts (aggregates, domain events), optimistic concurrency, and CQRS

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU and disk bound operations)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source software stack via Docker Compose)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Node.js 18+, Docker 24+, and Docker Compose installed
environment.fallback_path: SQLite in-memory append-only event table and Node.js EventEmitter if Docker Kafka cannot run

riskiest_component.name: Long Aggregate Replay Latency on Entities with Many Events
riskiest_component.fallback: Enforce automatic snapshot generation every 100 events to cap maximum replay length to 100 items

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an Event Sourcing and CQRS engine in TypeScript with append-only event store, optimistic concurrency, snapshots, and temporal queries.
worksheet.q2: Target users: distributed systems engineers, backend architects, and enterprise platform developers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: banking immutable audit trails, supply chain custody tracking, and DDD domain state reconstruction.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 39 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 34 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 39.1 -> 39 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: optimistic concurrency control in event store, exactly-once read projections, sub-15ms aggregate rehydration, and temporal replay.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 500 aggregate entities, 50,000 historical events across 5 domain event types. Synthetic records only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: SQLite in-memory mode.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Long replay latency on entities with many events. Fallback: snapshot every 100 events to bound replay to 100 items.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: mock state storage. Anti-fake check 5 appends 5 dynamic events at runtime and asserts temporal state match at step 3 vs step 5.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; synthetic business aggregates only.
